correctness.rationale: For T_n=L(K_n), n>=3, the p-pebble invariant explicitly maintains a bijection between underlying root endpoints of at most p pebbled edges. After recycling, <=2(p-1) endpoints remain and both n>=2p models have at least two fresh endpoints. This preserves graph vertex equality and adjacency at arbitrary depth. The same invariant survives a p-round ordinary Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse game. For each root cutoff 4<=s<=2p, a disjoint union of c=s-r nonempty paths with r=min(p,s-1) edges requires exactly s root vertices in every induced line-graph realization: nonconsecutive path edges are disjoint and different components share no endpoints. Existential adjacency diagrams of rank/width <=p distinguish n=s-1 from n>=s. The p=1 and n=3 boundaries are correctly separate. Independent induced-graph path forest enumeration for p=2..4 and 9 cutoffs corroborated. Thus both equivalences and least distinguishing width/rank floor(m/2)+1 are proved, not inferred from finite tests.
